utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we proceed with the witness, the Trial Chamber would like to hand down a ruling regarding the oral motion by the Defence on the use of the guilty plea by Mrs. Plavsic by the Prosecution. The oral motion was made on the 8th of April. The Trial Chamber is of the view that it does not require the documents sought by the Defence in their oral motion for them to challenge any evidence adduced by the Prosecution when using the guilty plea by Mrs. Plavsic. The Defence can examine their witnesses just as they do -- can re-examine their witnesses, just as they do with every other piece of evidence or exhibit produced by the Prosecution. The production of documents enumerated by the Defence in this regard is unnecessary, as it is not our role to inquire into or evaluate the merits of the plea and the sentencing judgement. The oral motion is therefore denied. We can now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Lazarevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Topolovac.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be brought closer to the microphones?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness move closer to the microphone so the interpreters can pick every word?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolovac, three days ago, we broke off your testimony because of the time was up. The last thing that we talked about just to remind you was that you said that apart from Mr. Stevan Todorovic, who was the only one authorised and who was the only one who took decisions as to who would be arrested and released from the police station and also that none other of the members of the police, be it commander or inspectors, had such powers. Do you remember that, saying that, when we adjourned?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to these topics, there were only a couple of things more that I wanted to ask you about, and that is what I will do now. Were there any instances when the so-called specials or those many-coloured as many people called them, did they also arrest people, bring them to the police station, to the TO building?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were instances where specials from Serbia brought and detained people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question on the same subject. Did anyone from the 4th Detachment ever arrest and detain people?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody, because I was there and I know the members of the 4th Detachment because they come from the town. I never observed any one of them -- any of the members of the 4th Detachment bring people to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I'd like to move on to a specific event and I'd like to hear from you what you know about it. So far, before this Chamber, it has mostly not been contested that that happened on the 26th of April, and that that day in the yard of the building housing the TO, one of those specials from Serbia, nicknamed Lugar, whose full name was Slobodan Miljkovic, killed a man whose nickname was Dikan. Can you tell me now what do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in the police station at the time but I did not see how that happened. I heard, and Simo Zaric was also in the police station and he said, as far as I can interpret it in my words, that lunatic killed a man in front of everybody. Simo was very upset and very angry because of what had happened, and said something needs to be done, meaning so as to remove people from that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now this: You say that Simo Zaric was upset. Could you personally see what he looked like or is it what you concluded from his -- from the tone of his voice?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both. The way he looked, attested to that, and also the tone that he used when he said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Did you perhaps see where Simo Zaric went?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. He went upstairs to the upper floor and stayed there a short while, and I assume that he was making some phone calls. After that, he returned, he went out of the room and the police station, and then came back after about an hour and a half or two maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I now only -- now tell me, but answer please only with yes or no, if you can. When is it that you saw him personally?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now tell me, was there anyone else at the time when you met Zaric there?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Savo Cancarevic was there and I was there and the inspectors were right next to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one thing to make the transcript quite clear. What office did Savo Cancarevic hold in the police station at that time, at that time, that is the 26th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to the 26th and then Savo Cancarevic was the commander of the police station, so he held the office of the station commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me this: Did you and Mr. Savo Cancarevic talk about something with Zaric? What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did, but before that I heard Simo turn to Savo Cancarevic as the commander, as the chief of the police station, and tell him not to put any spanners in the wheels and that he and I should help him in organising the transfer of people from the Territorial Defence building to the barracks in Brcko. Both of us accepted that and understood that in the TO building, some ugly things were happening, apart from physical harassment, that is there was even a murder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When that was said, that the prisoners should be transferred to the barracks in Brcko, can you tell me if Simo Zaric perhaps mentioned the names of the military who were to organise this and who were behind it?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before that, he said that he had talked with the superior officers, that is his superior officers, and at that moment, he mentioned the name of Momcilo Petrovic, nicknamed Pejo [phoen], and Paja [phoen] Meljenkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I didn't want to interrupt you but tell me, do you perhaps know what duties did Momcilo Petrovic and Paja Meljenkovic discharge in the Brcko barracks, what offices did they hold?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that, I remember that he mentioned that he had talked with them because they were his superiors and that the transfer of those people could be -- could take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will ask you some very specific questions, some questions very much to the point with regard to what you and Mr. Cancarevic did in the police station concerning the transfer of the prisoners to Brcko. First tell me if a list of prisoners was made?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Detainees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Detainees, thank you. And if so, who did that list?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received the list from the chief of the police station, Savo Cancarevic. Who made the list and when, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So Mr. Cancarevic gave you the list of prisoners and now tell me what did you do with that list?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the list and with Simo Zaric we went to the Territorial Defence building where the detainees were, and I took the list with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell me: When -- while you still were in the police building, in the SUP building, did you see any of the arrested persons?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I saw Sulejman Tihic in passing. He was on the upper floor in the police station building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell me now, as far as you can remember, how many people were there on that list that Savo Cancarevic gave you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact number but around 50 detainees. There were about 50 of them on that list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now tell me, did at some point arrive the military police and some JNA officers and some military vehicles and did they fetch up in front of the TO building and the police station? Because they face one another, don't they?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened before that, and I remember when we came with the list to the room where the detainees were in the TO building, then Simo told everybody standing in the doorway that they would leave that place and go to a safer place. Those present, to those present he said, "We must hurry," but that they should rest assured that they were going to a safer place because the building of the Territorial Defence itself did not really have the wherewithal for the stay of these people. I mean, the sanitary equipment was deficient, the building was pretty fragile and so on and so forth, and it could have been dangerous for them if they stayed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. But my question was whether military vehicles and the military police and some JNA officers come to the TO.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime, a truck arrived and it parked at the entrance into the yard of the Territorial Defence building and naturally the military police were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now: Did you perhaps know any of those soldiers who arrived then?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the truck arrived and it was parked at the entrance to the TO with Mr. Zaric, you've already told us what he had said to the detainees. Now tell me what happened next?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When everybody was out in the yard, that is after they had left the room and come out into the yard, I held the list and called out -- called out the names and those called out then boarded the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: As you were calling out those names and as those people boarded the truck, could you see any marks of physical harassment on them?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were some who could barely make it on to the truck or just couldn't, and I also saw my neighbour, Suad Grga [as interpreted], who looked beaten up, and who barely made it on to the truck and I don't think he realised where he was or where he was going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: How did this procedure go, at a normal pace, or was there any haste or how?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everything was in a rush. Zaric would say now and then, "Hurry up, hurry up, move on, move on."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me why was that, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because when Savo Zaric spoke to Cancarevic and me, he said that we have to carry out this action very quickly because the specials, that is the many-coloured might turn up and because that might spell trouble.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just one more question in relation to this: When this action was carried out, I mean when the transfer took place, when the truck arrived or people were called out and boarded the truck, tell me, were there any specials in the police station at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that time. At that time none were there. I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lazarevic, I would just like to clarify one thing with Mr. Topolovac. On page 7, line 14, you're talking about your neighbour who you saw, who looked beaten up and who barely made it on to the truck. Was that Mr. Grga Zubak, because in the transcript it says Suad Grga.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour I will clarify this with the witness. I apologise I cannot follow at the same time what the witness is talking and the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Topolovac, in the transcript, it says Suad Grga. That's what is in the transcript, so can you please repeat the name?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name is Grga Zubak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Grga Zubak was a member -- was in the TO, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was in the building of the TO, in a room in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have to clarify because my question was not properly recorded because here it says Grga Zubak was a member, was in the TO because this could possibly imply that he was a member of the TO and we know already that -- so I would just like that my question that I posed to the witness, if it could be recorded properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you don't have -- you've already answered but I just want my question to be recorded. Was Grga Zubak in the building of the TO, detained there?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was detained in the TO building. He wasn't a member of the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now tell me, after people called out from the list got on to the truck, did this truck leave?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were not one of the escorts of the truck?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I stayed at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Savo Cancarevic perhaps leave with this truck to escort it?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And neither Mr. Zaric, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'd like us to move on to the next day, that is the day after the transfer of prisoners to Brcko. Tell me, did you see Stevan Todorovic, and if you did, tell us what happened when you met him?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, and I remember that around 11.00 that day, when he came to the police station, he was angry and he was on edge. He raised his voice, and saying, "Who is Simo Zaric to transfer people from the TO building? Who is that Simo? Who is that 4th Detachment of his?" And he also rudely addressed me, said, "What are you, who do you think you are?" And he also spoke to the inspectors, "Who do you think you are to make something like that possible?" I mean the words that he used were brutal, he said you've only helped balijas and Ustasha and the like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already told us what were the relations between Mr. Zaric and Mr. Todorovic before that but now just tell me whether this event, the transfer of the detainees from TO to the barracks in Brcko, did that in any way affect the relations between Mr. Zaric and Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did. Their relations deteriorated, they became worse, that is. That is, between Stevan Todorovic and Simo Zaric, the relations became worse, in terms of intolerance on the part of Mr. Zaric with regard to Mr. Todorovic, because Todorovic always -- was always sorry that Simo Zaric would not be subjected to his control and so on and so forth because Simo Zaric never really worked in the police station except that he came on a couple of occasions, otherwise he was in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are now coming to the end of this area of examination. In your statement of mid -- you said that in mid-June, 1992, you said that you left the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you joined the military unit?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me what your personal attitude was to this event, your leaving the police and joining the army?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean my personal attitude?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I may not have phrased my question well. How did you experience this transfer from the police to the army as a human being? Was it a relief? Did you regret leaving the police?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the way the police worked was something I would never regret leaving. I hoped that they would work as I had worked in the police always in accordance with the law and with regulations, but unfortunately, this wasn't so, because Stevan Todorovic was a man who had no experience and who didn't care perhaps about police work. He was always surrounded by these specials. He spoke in a disjointed way. On the following day, he called me, not to the office but to the communications centre in the police station building, and he said, "Either you will work the way I tell you to or you will leave here." And by what he said, he simply threw me out. When I saw Vlado Sarkanovic who had already left two days previously, I asked him to transfer me back to the 4th Detachment. He helped me, and that's when I parted ways with Stevan Todorovic. I don't know how clear this is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's quite clear but, sir, because we are talking about June, there is no doubt that this is no longer the 4th Detachment but the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There was a transformation and you are right. It was the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination by the Prosecution? Cross-examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolovac, David Re is my name. I'm going to ask you some questions from the Prosecution. I just want you to listen very carefully to the questions I ask and please answer them as briefly as you possibly can. You understand all those things?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolovac, a moment ago you said you were transferred from the -- you were transferred back into the 4th Detachment, it was clarified you actually went into the Army of the Republika Srpska, the VRS. Just very briefly, on this issue, when you went into the army of the VRS, did you retain the 4th Detachment uniform and weapons and all equipment that had been issued to you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't transferred. I simply was expelled by Stevan Todorovic, and then I asked Vlado Sarkanovic to help me and he did help me join the ranks of the Army of Republika Srpska but the rest is correct. I did have a uniform of the Army of Republika Srpska and my personal weapons. I had nothing to do with the police station any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is simply this: You were in the 4th Detachment before you went to work at the police station, had a JNA 4th Detachment uniform and a weapon issued to you and some equipment, didn't you? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were working at the police station, did you keep your uniform, weapons and equipment at home and when you were expelled from the police station, did you put your uniform back on, keep your weapon and join the VRS unit?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned my weapons and my uniform, my 4th Detachment uniform, and when I arrived in the police station, I was wearing civilian clothes. I remember this well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I stop you? I'm only asking you about what happened when you left the police station. It's just quite brief, quite simple. You said a moment ago, you kept your -- I think there is confusion as to what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe my colleague would just divide his question in three questions and this would probably simplify, when you came to the police did you turn back your weapons and your uniform, after you went out from the police did you receive new uniform, it's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolovac I don't want to spend too long on this I just want to find out about when you went into the VRS. When you went into the VRS from the police station, did you still have the uniform of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You still had it at home and your weapon at home and the equipment at home while you were working at the police station? That's all I want to know. Or did you return them before you went to work at the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned them before I went to work at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, your evidence was of your working at the police station from April -- from -- in April 1992, several days after the takeover of Bosanski Samac. I just want to ask you some questions about your duties at the police station. In your statement at paragraph 19, you referred to your duties as being record-keeping. And you described these records as --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, maybe he could have his statement before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course, I'm sorry. I thought he had it there. I'm sorry. Do we have a copy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What's the problem? The statement dated 9/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I missed that. I haven't got written down in front of me, the exhibit number. Mr. Leese is looking for it. The exhibit number of the 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is D39/4. If you're referring to the witness's 92 bis statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolovac, can you just please turn to paragraph 19, just so you've got it in front of you. There is nothing controversial about what I'm going to ask you. I'm not trying to trick you any way. I'm just referring to what you said there to cast your mind to the evidence which is contained there. In your statement you referred to the keeping of records that you were asked to do, that is records of people who were brought in, work sheets, records of newly admitted members of the police and other regular SJB records. That's what's in your statement. Where -- were those in fact your duties, once you started work in the police station, the record keeping?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I arrived in the police station, Cancarevic, Savo, spoke to me and told me I would stay at the police station, bearing in mind that I was familiar with this kind of work, and that I would be in charge of the records you have mentioned in the police station. He said I would not be sent out on the ground and I spent my time keeping records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When I asked you before to be as brief as possible, it's already in your statement that that's what you did. All I'm asking you is if in fact that is what you did. So please -- I know it's difficult but please concentrate on the exact question I'm asking you, if possible. You did the record duty. Was that your job for the two months or so that you worked in the police station, record keeping?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you have -- did you work from an office?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your office, Mr. Topolovac?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Downstairs on the ground floor, when you go from the duty room, you pass through an office facing or looking on to the River Sava, if you know where that is. It was the second office to the left from the duty room, downstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was downstairs and was it in a place that enabled you to see everyone who was coming and going into the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was in the depth of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your job was record keeping and you said it was to keep records -- your evidence in the statement is to keep records of newly admitted members of the police and people who were brought in. Were you keeping records of prisoners as they were brought into the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning, yes, but later on, it was the duty service that did that, because I had to have a break, I had to go home to sleep and so on, and people were brought in at different times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was your responsibility, is that what you're saying, to keep the records of the prisoners who were detained in Mr. Todorovic's custody, although of course you couldn't do it when you physically weren't at the station. Are you saying it was your responsibility to keep the records but when you weren't there because you were at home, someone else did your duties?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work every day in the police station between when you started in April and when you were expelled in mid-June?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But sometimes I was absent because I was on leave. Mostly yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say leave you're talking about Sundays or Saturdays or what? Were you able to say how many days you weren't there over that two month period, doing as best as you can?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly one day in the week I was off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the only person designated to maintain the records, that is were you the person in charge of maintaining the records of the Bosanski Samac SUP for those two months?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was also Milan Jekic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you share the duties of record maintenance or responsibility for record maintenance?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said Milan Jekic was also in charge of maintaining the records. Who was the person primarily responsible for maintaining the records, that is the records officer of the station? Was it you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Records recorded prisoners brought in. Did they also record prisoners leaving the station?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they --

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they record deaths of prisoners in custody?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first and the second records were kept by the duty service, because it was they who were able to monitor this, so that was their task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just clarify what you mean by first and second records and duty service, just those three things, please?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Release. When a person was brought in, if Stevan Todorovic decided he was to be released, the duty service had to make a record of this. Also, if a detainee fell ill or died, it was the duty service who was in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the duty service? Could you also please clarify that for us?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty service was in charge of surveillance of the detainees, reports by citizens, keeping records of people detained also, and other tasks they were charged with by Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the records of interrogations of prisoners, the files relating to the interrogations of the prisoners who were interrogated there? Did you keep those records or did someone else keep those records?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't accessible to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about records of people visiting or entering the police station. When you worked there before the war, were records kept of visitors, that is visitors to prisoners, military people, or perhaps police or SJB people from other districts? Were records kept of them coming to the police station and who they saw?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that such records were kept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in charge of record keeping for those two months in 1992, were records kept of people in those categories, such as military personnel, other police from other districts, civilian officials who weren't police officers coming to the police station to see prisoners or for any other business?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the defendant or the sorry the accused, Dr. Blagoje Simic, at the Bosanski Samac police station in the two months that you worked there?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mr. Miroslav Tadic? Did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you keep records of the prisoners who were removed or transferred to Brcko in April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That list was given back to the commander, Savo Cancarevic. There was a list, as I said, it had already been made. It was handed to me by Savo Cancarevic and after reading out the names, I returned it to the station chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did -- where were you when Savo Cancarevic handed you this list, Mr. Topolovac?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upstairs on the upper floor, at the place where his office is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was near to where Mr. Tihic was being detained, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cancarevic, he was present -- was he present when the prisoners were actually transferred, the physical putting them on to the trucks and so on?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think he was upstairs, Zaric and I were there. I can't remember. He may have been standing behind my back, but a lot of time has elapsed. It's possible that he may have been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any reason you know of for him to give you the list, and say, "Mr. Topolovac," or whatever he called you, "I want you to read the list out"? Is there any reason he couldn't have done it himself if it was his list?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've known Mr. Zaric for a long time, haven't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's a long-term friend of yours, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both of you were unhappy about what was happening in the SUP, in the period you worked there, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And both of you talked about it during that period, that is April to June, 1992, when you were working there?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object. I object. I mean that the evidence of the witness was very clear as what the period was where he saw Mr. Zaric in the police station and June was not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was both of you talked about it during that period. You don't have to talk about it in the police station. I don't understand the objection. The witness must be able to answer whether he spoke to Mr. Zaric during that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mentioned that the period --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If this is the question, I have no objection, just to divide some period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand the question, Mr. Topolovac, in the period you worked in the police station you talked to Mr. Zaric about your concerns, your mutual concerns about what was happening there, that's over that two month period, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not that two month period. It refers to the period when that person was killed. That's when there was talk of this, and in early May, Simo Zaric left the police station and after that I didn't see him very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did Mr. Zaric speak to you, as far as you know, or say hello to you, as far as you know, every time he came to the police station, in the period you worked there? I mean as far as you know did he drop in and say, "Hello, I'm here"? Talk to you about anything?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but Simo is someone who was always polite, who always said hello, but I was in the back part of the building, so I didn't see him every time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's entirely possible that he came to the police station every day for two to three hours between the period when you first started working there and the 1st of May without your knowing that he was there? Is that what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's -- the way that the question is posed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The question was posed, I don't know how the witness could answer, yes of course there is such possibility. He already said that. But I don't know why he's insisting on this every day because, all right, maybe the witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness can answer according to the way he understood the question. You don't have to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer to the question was it's not possible. What you're saying is you would have known if Mr. Zaric was in the police station because he was a polite person you would have expected him to have greeted you as a courtesy?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, every time, if, that is, he saw me, but his every visit during that period of time that you tell us, he could spend there three hours without me being able to see him and greet him. Simo could have come several times during that period, perhaps five or six times, and later on, in early May, I did not see him come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your evidence this morning was you saw him a couple of times, your evidence on Monday was that you saw him in the police station five or six times. All I'm something you've given two different, two different numbers, figures, for the number of times you saw him during that period.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said several times, and in my book, it means five or six times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The translation we got a little bit earlier this morning was a couple of times, a couple, as far as I understand in English, means two. Are you saying that you said something different, several, meaning -- five or six?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is just a problem of interpretation in our language there isn't much difference between several and couple. There is what we receive in translation, it's words "nekoliko" and it could mean couple and several.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to ask the witness what he meant by couple, or several, was it five or six or how many times, because we have had two distinct, in the English translation, at least, figures given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you understand what I am saying, I am just trying to -- there seems to be difference, it might be translation, we got a couple meaning two and you said on Monday five or six. When you said a couple or several, did you in fact mean five or six or did you mean something else?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant five or six times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Zaric gave an interview to the Office of the Prosecution in June -- sorry, the 2nd of April, 1998, which is in evidence. It's P141 ter, for the record. And at page 32, he said that in that period, that is from the takeover to the 1st of May, 1992, I was going to the SUP for about two or three hours of the day, sorry, two or three hours a day, I'm sorry, the rest of the time I was in the field and visiting units and carrying out the tasks that I had to do. Knowing Simo Zaric as you do, long term friend, do you have any reason to disbelieve his own version in evidence that he was there for two or three hours every day in that period?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, for -- to be fair to the witness, maybe he could take a look at this portion of Mr. Zaric's interview, because it is not that well translated, as we receive now the translation of this portion of his interview. It's actually page 33 and I already underlined this part of his interview and I can show it to the witness, if the Trial Chamber finds it's appropriate, because there are a couple of words before this quotation that the Prosecution made and we believe that it's a bit changes the meaning of the words in a way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can you -- since you have the page, can you say what the words are?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: First of all, when quoting Mr. Zaric, and I will read it in B/C/S, [Interpretation] "I approximately, perhaps, dropped to -- in the SUP for two or three hours [Realtime transcript read in error "days"] a day but only in daytime." [In English] Actually it's two or three hours. Here I see in the translation, for two or three days. And it said, and in our language, when it says [Interpretation] a day, [In English] it doesn't mean necessarily every day. So it means that if he comes on one day he would stay two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May I ask Mr. Re, we are spending so much time on this, because the point is Mr. Simo Zaric from the interview does say he used to go to the police station, whatever number of times a day. The witness has said how many times he saw him at the police station, and he has explained that because his office was in a certain place in the building, he might not have seen him every time that the witness -- that Mr. Simo Zaric went to the police, to the SUP, so I don't understand the point of pursuing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I won't pursue it. I will just note for the record that the objection taken has never been made. We have asked witnesses before in relation to that particular passage. It's been in evidence since I think September last year, that objection has never been taken to the translation until this point. We could easily have had it retranslated if there was a problem had it been brought to our attention on the other occasions we have raised this with witnesses but I won't take it any further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement at paragraph 18, sir, you said when you first came to the police station there were -- there was a man in -- in camouflage uniform who spoke to me, raising his voice, said, who are you, man, what are you play acting here while another one said put your uniform on quickly or else. That's in your statement. What uniform were they referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 18, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you in fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, maybe -- I just want to -- I can ask that in redirect but are you referring to the uniform that this gentleman was wearing or the uniform that he should have worn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which he had on. That's what he meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that's fairly apparent. Now, Mr. Topolovac, you said he was referring to the camouflage uniform. Did you in fact wear a uniform or put one on when you were working in the police station, as a result of that conversation? That's all I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in civilian --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic was in charge of the station. That's in your statement and in your evidence. And I think you're saying that he was the person who governed access to the station; is that correct? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means of course that he was the person who allowed military people like Simo Zaric to come in to interrogate prisoners? Did you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did. Well, yes, that is what one can conclude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, you know Mr. Zaric conducted some interviews in the police station. Were you present when he conducted any of these interviews?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If I may go back to your previous question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly, sir. The question was Todorovic -- just hang on, Todorovic was in charge of the police station, he was the one who governed access, that is anyone, including the military, and Mr. Zaric, to come in and go -- and interrogate prisoners. That was the question and you said yes, that would be the conclusion. Do you wish to add something to it?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to add that I am not aware of that but Stevan Todorovic himself decided whom he would let in and whom he wouldn't let in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, from your working there in those two months, Mr. Zaric would not have been able to come in and interrogate prisoners in Todorovic's custody without Todorovic allowing him to do so or giving orders to others to allow him to do so, could he?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know what the understanding regarding that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, people just couldn't walk in off the street, could they, and go and start interrogating prisoners? They had to have permission of the person running the station, didn't they? It couldn't have happened otherwise, could it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: True, but I never saw such a permit. Perhaps it existed, perhaps it was verbal or in writing, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I'm saying to you is from your experience, the evidence you gave, of Todorovic being in charge giving orders as to who was arrested, who was detained, who was released, it was his police station, and from your experience of working there and what you saw, Mr. Zaric could not have come in and interrogated prisoners without Mr. Todorovic allowing him access to do so, could he?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The "yes" is a little bit ambiguous. When you say "yes," do you mean no, Mr. Zaric could not have come in without Mr. Todorovic's permission?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not really know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of anyone who was able to come in and interrogate prisoners or had access to prisoners without the express permission of Todorovic or people acting under his orders during the two months that you were there?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was giving -- you said Todorovic was in charge. He gave orders in relation to arrests and imprisonment. Did he give orders to a duty officer to assemble squads of mixed paramilitary or special volunteers and local police to go out and search for particular people?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Stevan Todorovic did give such orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is some evidence before the Court, Mr. Topolovac, that it was in fact you who compiled the list or you with Mr. Cancarevic who compiled the list of prisoners to be transferred to Brcko. In fact, Mr. Zaric in his record of interview at -- that's P141, could the witness please be shown P141, that's ter, at page 44?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just tell you what it says and then you'll have a chance to read it for yourself to save some time. The question was, of the Prosecutor to Mr. Zaric --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think let the witness have the document first.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document be put on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go to page 45, please, sir, can you see at the top of the page where it says, I'm sorry if you could just go over the page before, please just go back over the page before, that's my mistake, to page 44, please go back a page?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, just a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just go back a page.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given the document in English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Yugoslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise for that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have it in B/C/S now. Can you please go to page 44? You'll see there is English and Yugoslav there. The bottom of the page, the question is Nancy --

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... TO and SUP were transferred to Brcko, how was it decided who got transferred to Brcko and who stayed behind? Now, the answer is over the page, and it's Mr. Zaric, Mr. -- it was Savo Cancarevic who was the police commander at that time, and Mr. Topolovac, who was his deputy. They had compiled the list and I didn't have anything to do with it. They decided who should go and Mr. Topolovac read out the list after it was done and the prisoners were put in the vehicles, then I left the building of the TO, I'm only talking about the people in that one room in the TO building.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we have the document on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters would like to have the document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see the questions and answers the question of the Prosecutor, Nancy, and Mr. Zaric's answer saying it was you and Mr. Cancarevic who compiled the list. I'm just going to ask you do you know of any reason why Mr. Zaric would say that if it wasn't correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the text be moved up, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know. Perhaps that's what he thought but I remember well that Savo gave me the list that he had made. Now, how -- I didn't have a hand in making the list. I got the list from Savo Cancarevic, the chief of the station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there is also evidence before the Court that the list was compiled upstairs opposite where Mr. Tihic was and Mr. Zaric was there at the time, as was Captain Petrovic. There was you, Mr. Zaric and Captain Petrovic and that you dictated the list for the benefit of the Trial Chamber that's at T 1446. I just want to suggest that that's in fact what happened. That you were -- it was either you or someone else who dictated -- sorry, that you were the person that dictated the list in the presence of Mr. Zaric and Captain Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. That can be removed, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is also evidence before the Court, Mr. Cancarevic [sic], that Mr. Todorovic was in fact there on the night of the transfer, possibly for about ten minutes or so. I want to suggest to you that he was in fact there for a short period of time when the transfer was going on, and he didn't interfere.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zaric has written a book called, "On The Hague cross." Have you read his book, Mr. Topolovac?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In his book, this is at page 176 of the English, he said that "We heard from Savo Cancarevic, who was then police chief in Samac and Topolovac, his deputy, that `the head honchos' had approved the entire list. They had accepted it obviously with no suspicions and commented let them have all the assholes they have asked for and throw in three labourers too but no more than three." They themselves decided which three. That's what Mr. Zaric said in the book you read about your role in compiling the list and putting names on it. Do you have any reason to doubt the accuracy of that?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true that Savo Cancarevic was the chief of the police station, no never. And me as his deputy, so it is either a misprint or an error made during writing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric in the book, page 176, the book that you read, said "The list he -- he had some part in this with Mr. Maksimovic, meaning Makso Simeunovic, about some reports he'd written and he said the next day, Maksimovic phoned me and said he had told `the boss' everything. He too agrees that something has to be done. Especially since the army needs some of those men for additional clarification of some matters, especially in connection with the illegal arming and instances of sabotage against the JNA as in Brcko, for example. I, that's Simo Zaric, was not able to tie up all `loose ends' on the basis of the material I had been given and the suspects I had interrogated, nor was I able to figure out things related to Sijekovac, Bosanski Brod and Derventa. I did not know what else they had especially as regards cases in which some JNA members were involved or suspected. They would not tell me whether the mysterious major whom I met in Todorovic's office while I was interrogating Tihic was working on that. He could have been from counterintelligence, something that Maksimovic and Nikolic may after all have known. The boss, he said, would talk to the people in the town and see if at least the men we needed could be pulled out and kept in more decent conditions. Are the others not human beings, I asked, that's Zaric, I asked, we should do something for them too." A few paragraphs down, "Two days later, it was already arranged for the army to take over the men `it needed.' Thanks in the first place to Maksimovic's understanding we had extended the list as much as we could. And included in it many names apart from the men whom I had interrogated and a few more cases were being investigated by others. We added those whom we knew to be in detention and in a bad state as well as a few men we trusted knowing them to be honest." And so on. That's when he gets to the bit about Petrovic and the comment that "Let them have all the assholes they have asked for and throw in three labourers too." Now my question is that's a book you've read, your name appears in it, it's a description -- I'll just finish the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I found it very hard to follow what you were quoting. First of all, we didn't have the accurate translation and I believe that the interpreters already addressed to us and us saying that they don't have the text of this book before them so they can make an accurate translation. Second, it was a very long quotation. I would really like to see what was -- what would be the result of this quotation and the question finally posed to the witness because there are so many things in this quotation. There are literally at least 20 topics raised in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course I'm quite happy to show the witness the passage from the book which isn't in evidence yet but I intend to tender it. I was just reading it to him to allow him to know what Mr. Zaric, the book he's read, said about the account the witness has given and ask him to comment on it. I'm finished the quotation. I'm of course quite happy to give him a copy of the relevant page to look at but my question was going to be having heard that, do you have any reason to disbelieve Mr. Zaric's account in his book, the accuracy of it? It's simply that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the witness can tell the Trial Chamber whether or not he followed the quotation and whether or not he understood it. And then he can answer the question posed by the Prosecution. Because as the Prosecution says, this is a book that the witness has read.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's actually 10.30, Your Honour. It's 10.32 actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes, we have gone past our break. We shall continue our proceedings at 1100 hours. Judge Lindholm was just suggesting that perhaps the pages could be handed over to the witness and then he can peruse them during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolovac, the Court -- I'm sorry, just before I do that, during the break, the interpreters approached me and in relation to those two translation issues they said that the word "couple" -- the witness used the word "couple." It has a specific meaning in B/C/S, meaning two, as in English, and then used the word later "several" and the word "several" means two or three, it doesn't mean five or six and they said in relation to the translation of the word a day, P141 at page 32, as appears translated is the day, it's not in daytime, it means very strictly each day. That was the translation the interpreters approached me and told me about it during the break. So I've placed those matters on the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolovac, the Court -- the Court actually gave you a copy of the relevant pages from Mr. Zaric's book. You've had a chance to read them over the last 15 or 20 minutes, I take it? Have you read it? That's all I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You've read the book before and you've got no reason to disbelieve Mr. Zaric's account in his published book of the reason for the removal being for -- of some of the people being for further interrogation, for military purposes, at Brcko, have you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, when you say yes, do you mean no, you have no reason to disbelieve or yes, you do have a reason to disbelieve?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to disbelieve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have no reason to disbelieve Mr. Zaric's account there of the way it was organised or what actually happened, do you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor do you have any reason to disbelieve his version of the comment which he says you made or you and Cancarevic made about "let them have all the assholes they have asked for and throw in the three labourers too but no more than three." They themselves decided the three. You have got no reason to disbelieve that version in his published book, which you've read do you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also on this, on the last page which you have in front of you, that's page 178 in the English, and page 245 in the Yugoslav, as you called it, where Mr. Zaric said in relation to their transfer from Brcko to Bijeljina, "and so it was they were transferred from Brcko to Bijeljina, why some of them were later moved to Batajnica and others to Sremska Mitrovica and what had prompted all these wanderings, I can only guess. They could have done something against the JNA which could have necessitated further investigation, a follow-up to what had been initiated in Samac. I do not think there was time to wrap up any such thing in Brcko. I'm willing to believe and indeed I am sure that it was better for them to be as far away from Samac as possible." I just note I have provided the interpreters with copies, French, B/C/S and English of the passages that I'm reading from in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, first of all, this witness accordingly to his statement and what he stated here before this Tribunal, has absolutely no knowledge that these were transferred somewhere to Bijeljina or after Brcko. And even in this quotation that Mr. Re made, there is also one sentence here that says that even Mr. Zaric's assuming something, speculates on something, and I really don't know how could this witness answer and give any comment regarding this part of the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's really in relation to the words, a follow-up to what had been initiated in Samac. I was only reading the rest of the paragraph to put it in context. It's only in relation to those. The initiation of what happened in Samac, the question is simply, you have no reason to disbelieve what Mr. Zaric said there about what was initiated in Samac and what happened afterwards, do you sir,? That's as far as I wish to take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before the witness answers, regarding Mr. Lazarevic's intervention, all I can say is that this witness was there, he knows what happened, and then he has read this book, and the questions are clear from the Prosecution, so he can answer the best way he understands the questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolovac, you understand my question, you've read the passage, my question is simply having read it, having read the book, you've got no reason to disbelieve what Mr. Zaric said in that paragraph in relation to what was initiated in Samac and he says should have been followed up elsewhere, do you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, again, that's slightly ambiguous. It's not your fault. When you said "yes" you mean you've got no reason to disbelieve him. Could you just say I've got no reason to disbelieve him if that's what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, when I say that I have no reason to disbelieve, I don't know whether I said this, but it is my opinion that the transfer of the detainees was done by Simo for their own good, and that in this way, he saved the lives of many detainees in the TO building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you that. I'm just trying clarify an ambiguity. When I said you I had no reason to disbelief, it said yes. I'll put it the other way around. Do you have any reason to disbelieve what he said in that paragraph? Yes, you do have a reason to disbelief or no, you have no reason to disbelieve? That's all I'm trying to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to disbelieve.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the tender of the book. I move to tender the book or that portion into evidence, should it be given an ID number at the moment or can we wait until after the witness is gone? It's a matter for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What I want to know is it's the whole book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's the whole book. The whole book has been translated and provided to us of course by the Defence, I believe. The passages we were relying upon were pages 175 through to 178 in the English and pages 242 to 245 in the B/C/S. I'm sorry, that's right, 242, 3, 4, 5, in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Re, before we do anything on that, could you just give the title of the book? Because I seem to remember this morning that the title you gave was slightly different to the title that was given before which I think was "Crucifixion in The Hague." And this morning you said something different so I would just like to be certain we are talking about the same book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The English translation, the title is "Crucified in The Hague." That's the official translation, first edition 1999. If I could just read the word in B/C/S sometimes it's translated as on "The Hague cross" meaning I suppose the Christian cross. Sometimes there is a slight difference, different people call it different things. The official translation says crucified. Perhaps if I just read the B/C/S or perhaps if this is put on the ELMO for the interpreters to see they could give --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think Mr. Lazarevic can assist us with that. What is the official title in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will gladly do that. The official --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I mean what's the book called, that's all?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Official title is [Interpretation] "On The Hague crucifixion." [In English] Crucifixion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Fine is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours I have no problem with this but in this proceedings, we already have a couple of times some issues regarding books of witnesses. We are all aware that we had one situation with the book of Mr. Sulejman Tihic and then after that, there were other books by Mr. Dragan Lukac and Dragan Delic who were all witnesses before this Tribunal. And the ruling of the Trial Chamber, if I remember correctly, was that books written by people who will testify and give their testimony here viva voce are not acceptable into evidence since we already have people here who will testify about their own experience. They can be used for the purposes of -- well, I don't know, challenging some parts of the statement, and I believe that Mr. Zaric will give his testimony before this Tribunal. So I'm just concerned about the previous ruling of the Trial Chamber in the same situations. We have -- we face that situation at least three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the Trial Chamber will deal with the ruling later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I be heard? Not at the moment but on that particular issue at some point, not while the witness is here obviously. Before Your Honours rule I'll just ask that the Prosecution be heard. We haven't argued our case for its tender into at mission, not now I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So we will give you an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Lazarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Topolovac, I have only a couple of points to clarify that follow from the Prosecution questions and your replies. The Prosecutor asked you whether Stevan Todorovic had to approve the arrival of Simo Zaric to the police station and if I understood your reply correctly you said that you had not seen either written approval or heard oral approval by Stevan Todorovic and then the Prosecutor suggested that as Todorovic approved everything and was asked about everything, he probably had to have approved this as well, and then you agreed. I will now ask you whether you have any information and you already said this during the examination-in-chief, that is that Simo Zaric came there on orders from the commander, Commander Nikolic, and Radovan Antic. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So if somebody discussed this with Stevan Todorovic and agreed with him, it didn't necessarily have to be Simo Zaric, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, it could have been one of his superiors possibly with whom he had discussed this and agreed on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Re, the Prosecutor, now quoted certain parts of Mr. Zaric's book. And in one of your responses, you said that this had to be a mistake. Maybe a typing error or an error in the text, because Savo Cancarevic was never the chief of police. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you were given a part to read, and you noticed the name of an officer who is mentioned, and in the book it says his name is Maksimovic. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this part of the book, it says Maksimovic. That's what you read; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man called Makso Simeunovic, have you ever heard of such a man?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard of him but I've never seen him and I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there has been testimony before this Tribunal, and there are indications that it was Maksim Simeunovic who was the man who came on that occasion and took away the detainees from the TO. Do you have any reason to doubt this?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to this. This is cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'll allow the question, Mr. Re. The witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat. Do you have any reason to doubt that it was Makso Simeunovic, who came to collect the detainees from the TO? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me? Oh, I apologise. I thought you were speaking to the Prosecutor. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no reason to doubt this?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the book, however, it says Maksimovic, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we will agree on the basis of these two examples, that there are certain errors in the book which you yourself have just mentioned, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is imprecision in the book, either as a result --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I do object. This is a series of leading cross-examining questions to the witness. He can certainly be asked about any of these --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I withdraw, I withdraw, I withdraw, I withdraw. I have no further questions. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Topolovac, I just have a few questions for you. The first question is in order for any detained person to be released from the SUP, was the approval of Dr. Blagoje Simic also necessary, as well as that of the chief of police, Mr. Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you. Second question is do you know whether two detained persons, a Mr. Jusufovic and a Mr. Fadil Sabanovic, who were interrogated on the same day as Mr. Sulejman Tihic in the SUP, do you know whether Mr. Simo Zaric released these two gentlemen, Mr. Jusufovic and Mr. Sabanovic, if I'm pronouncing them correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you. The third question is, in the records in the police station, in the SUP, did these records show not only the name of the person who had been arrested and detained, but also the name or names of those persons who had made the arrest and brought them into the SUP?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the form, in the book of records, it said which patrol had brought the person in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. And last question is: Do you know, do you recall, the names of the people on the patrol that arrested Mr. Kemal Bobic?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Mr. Topolovac, at the time when some or part of the detainees were transferred to Brcko, do you have any picture of how many detainees there were at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say with any precision, but it was approximately that number, the number on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Which means that all the detainees were transferred to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: In that case, if all the detainees were transferred, why was it necessary to have them listed and called out from the list instead of just taking them down and put them on the truck?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's so that it would be known who was on the way there, who was sent there, so that if anything should happen during the transport, there would be a list of people who were being transported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: But if the list contained the names of all the detainees, why was it necessary to call them out by name, if nobody remained in custody?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what police work is like. You have to identify a person. You have to call out their name and then see whether that person actually boarded the bus or not. If a list was made, I see no reason not to call out the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: So to be quite sure on my point, your testimony is that all the detainees were transferred to Brcko and not just certain persons picked out and put on the list? Because you -- you gave testimony and one could also understand from the book written by Mr. Zaric that the list was compiled, which so to say is -- I understand it, I understood it the way that not all detainees were transferred but only certain picked out and put on the list.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO TOPOLOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that someone stayed behind, that not all of them got on the bus, but I didn't see that. It was night-time or late evening and we were working quite fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Well, I have no further questions. Thank you. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, thank four giving evidence to the Tribunal. We are finished with you. You may leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: While the witness is being brought in, Mr. Lazarevic, the Trial Chamber has been informed that you haven't taken any steps to have the Rule 92 bis statement of Mr. Ramusovic completed with formalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have to apologise for that.
