I was informed by the officer of the court and during the break I will make all necessary applications to the Registry, because I'm kindly asking for understanding, we are in the middle of our Defence case and I was mainly focused on witnesses and all the problems that we have with witnesses about their arrival and everything, and I will do the necessary application during next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I want to say that the reason the Tribunal pays for two lawyers on each case is precisely that they share the duties. Can we have the next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is on his way in, I had a brief discussion with chambers legal officer and the Registry about the Rule 71 deposition witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I -- Mr. Leese our case manager tells us that we only received the copies yesterday of the Rule 71 deposition transcripts. They came to the Prosecutor's Office yesterday, we haven't looked at them. I understand that the Registry has had them for sometime but our latest information and we have not seen them so I haven't been able to make the application I was going to make in relation to two witnesses but I will certainly go back to my office very soon, start reading them and file something very quickly. That's the reason for any perceived delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the Trial Chamber have had these transcripts for a long time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has been informed by the Registry assistant that in fact these transcripts were given to all the parties sometime back, more than three weeks ago. We will proceed with the witness. Can the witness make the solemn declaration, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Pisarevic? Examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Topcagic. I believe that the redacted version has already been handed to the members of the Chamber. And other participants in these proceedings. Mr. Topcagic, will you please state for the record your full name?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: My name is Fadil Topcagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your other particulars are in this statement which you made and certified in December in Bosanski Samac. So that now we shall talk about parts of your statement which were struck out from your statement as ruled by the Trial Chamber. During the preparation of your testimony, during your proofing, we talked about how it will be best technically to conduct this testimony and those instructions which I gave you on that occasion remain in force, which means listen to my question, wait a couple of seconds, then answer, try to -- try not to speak too fast so that the interpreters could interpret what you say, because the purpose of this is to have your testimony on record, the testimony that you will give to the best of your knowledge and recollection. If you find a question unclear, feel free to tell me so and I shall repeat it. In your statement, in passage in paragraph 39, and in some preceding paragraphs, you testified about what had gone on in Bosanski Samac, and about things that happened in the police station in Bosanski Samac on the -- in the morning of the 17th, and on which occasion a member of the many-coloured, as you put it, was wounded, the man whose nickname was or rather whom you knew only by his nickname, and that was Debeli, fatso, you took him to Crkvina to the cultural club. So tell us what happened after you arrived there, to the cultural centre in the village of Crkvina, whom did you find in that centre and what else happened there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in Crkvina, I had not known this man before until that morning, but people called him Debeli, fatso. In the cultural centre in Crkvina, I came across Blagoje Simic, physician, former deputy mayor of the municipality of Samac, and the president of the SDS. Before that, I helped that Debeli to enter the building and Dr. Simic helped him with the wound that he had in -- around his shoulder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Dr. Simic extended medical aid to him in relation to that wound that he had sustained?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present during that intervention?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you at some point address Debeli with a question?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. I asked where do I go now? And he said that I was free to leave the car in which we had arrived and to go to Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that car was that a police car that you had brought him to Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: It was a police car, it was a Zastava 11, white, but it did not have any markings, it did not say, "Police" for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn the name of that man whom you only knew as Debeli at the time later on?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did. His name was Srecko Radovanovic. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please it's unclear the evidence on this witness's knowledge of the name. Mr. Pisarevic has suggested that the witness knew the man as Debeli at the time he arrived at the cultural centre. However, it may not be the case. It may be that the witness is saying that he learnt of the name subsequently, after, in the following weeks and months. So if Mr. Pisarevic could clarify when it was that the witness knew the name of this paramilitary -- of Debeli, that would assist you, certainly assist the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think counsel can deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony, Mr. Topcagic, you said that that morning, on the 17th, you knew that person only by his nickname, Debeli.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much later did you find out his full name?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Well, it must have been not less than ten days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, you set off towards Samac and tell us where did you fetch up, which location, when you left Crkvina and arrived in Samac?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I started on foot from Crkvina and a man came up in a car, and I hitched a ride, and he left me off at the -- at the brickyard, at the entrance into Samac, or the so-called mouth of the Bosna, and then I continued on foot to SIT, where the 4th Detachment had its offices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean that the command of the 4th Detachment was in the SIT?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. The offices of the SIT housed the command of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at about what time did you get to the command of the 4th Detachment on the SIT premises?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: It was around 5.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to the command of the 4th Detachment, around 5.00 in the morning, in the SIT building, did you see anyone there? And if you did, who was that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: At the very exit from SIT, I met the commander of the 4th Detachment, Radovan Antic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please describe your encounter? Did you talk about anything?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I told them briefly what had happened to me this morning -- that morning. They looked worried, and asked me why had I not reported that night when I went to where I had been, why had I not called by telephone, and I said that I couldn't do it, that I was unable to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you told them what you had lived through that night, where you'd been and what you'd done, and when you saw them there at the exit, did you know, did they tell you where they were headed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: They said that they were off to see Lieutenant Colonel Stevan Nikolic, for a briefing to see what was to be done under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that conversation, was it short?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: It was very short, because they were in a hurry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you that you'd tell them all in detail after they returned?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Mr. Zaric and Mr. Antic left to Pelagicevo, what was there in Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: In Pelagicevo, were JNA troops or rather the technical, tactical group 17. Pelagicevo is 40 kilometres from Samac and was in the municipality of Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And who commanded the 17th Tactical Group of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: The commander of that 17th Tactical Group was Stevan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you arrived there and those two left, who else was there in the command? Whom did you see there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: By that time, 50 or thereabouts people had gathered there, members of the 4th Detachment, who did not know themselves what to do under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all armed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No. By and large -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm just wondering if the witness has a statement before him. I just notice he has an open document, and if he's testifying on these issues that have been redacted from his or taken out from his original statement, then he should be giving his evidence viva voce not by reference to or with the assistance of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. He shouldn't have his statement -- MR. DI FAZIO: Shouldn't have it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Unless it's the redacted one. Is it the redacted one? I mean the one where the paragraphs were struck out?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, indeed, the usher has given the gentleman, Mr. Topcagic, a redacted version, which we handed to the Chamber and the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is fine, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something? What I'm telling you is not that page at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nor is it in that statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nor is it in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Captain Jovo Savic the deputy commander there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about members of the detachment? Were they wearing the military uniforms of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk with members of the 4th Detachment who were in the command that morning about what was going on in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Those who had arrived in the command of the 4th Detachment had come across largish groups of armed Muslims around the mosque and the department store, the hotel, the marketplace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not armed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I wasn't armed, nor was I wearing any army clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why didn't you go home to get your weapons, the weapons that you had been issued with by the 4th Detachment and put on the uniform also issued by the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I did not go because for my safety, because that area was held by Muslim armed formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I get your meaning properly, your house, where your weapons were and where your uniform was, was in a part of the town where there were also armed groups of Muslim formations, is that it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when Mr. Zaric and Mr. Antic returned from Pelagicevo? When was that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: They returned sometime between 8.00 and 9.00, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the rest of the members of the 4th Detachment, you included, were they informed about the orders issued by the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you told then?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: They told us that the messengers should go off and bring together as many soldiers of the 4th Detachment as possible, as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So that was sometime between 8.00 and 9.00, and during that time, when -- during that time that they were in Pelagicevo, did members of the 4th Detachment come to the command post to -- just wait, please. Wait.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Members of the 4th Detachment did come to that command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember roughly how many of them had got there by 9.00?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Well, I'd say between 80 and 100 members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did commander Antic, Radovan Antic, issue any order to the members of the 4th Detachment that morning?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Sometime around 11.00 we were ordered to get hold of the boundary areas around Samac, next to the rivers Bosna and Sava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us, did you set off to carry out that combat assignment? Who led you and what did it look like? I mean taking the possession of those boundary areas in the town of Samac or rather the right banks of the rivers Bosna and Sava.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: We started cautiously and slowly, because houses were only about 2 or 3 metres away from the embankment and it was very likely that fire would be opened on us at our backs, that is, by members of Muslim formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. And those boundary areas of the town of Samac, are these defence dikes to prevent against flooding by the Bosna and the Sava?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. These are dikes which were put in place to defend against flooding by the Sava and the Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got there, were you deployed along those dikes on the side of the town with the view of the Sava and the Bosna and that is Croatia across these two rivers?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were deployed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did taking possession of these positions, how long did this assignment take?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Well, it took until about, well, maybe two hours, three hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you took positions on those dikes, or rather on that line, where did you stay, in which part, next to the Bosna or next to the Sava?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I stayed on the dike running along the Bosna River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day, was artillery, mortar fire, opened on the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Fire was opened from the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was fire opened by members of the Croat Defence Council who were on the left bank of the Bosna River?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That's right, but that was around or after 1700, in late afternoon, at dusk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, around 1700, did the unfettered crossing of civilians across the bridge on the River Bosna to the village of Brod [as interpreted] stop?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Until that gunfire, one could cross normally, whoever wanted to could cross, be it in a vehicle or on foot or by bicycle but when this fire started, then we would not let people go through because we were concerned about their safety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there nearby, near the bridge across the Bosna?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you spend that night, then?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: We spent that whole night on the dikes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do the next day, on the 18th of April, 1992? That is now we'll talk about things, about developments that took place on the 18th of April, 1992. What happened to you? Where did you go? Where were you invited to go?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, the command of the 4th Detachment was relocated and put up in the house of Ljubo [as interpreted] Dusanovic, who lived in Australia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that house in the locality?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That house was in the locality of sljivak, the plum orchard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just please don't hurry. Wait for me to finish my question, pause and then start your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Could I ask you a question, just for the transcript? On page 53, lines 18 and 19, especially line 19 you say across the bridge on the River Bosna, to the village of Brod. Shouldn't it be Prud?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just correct something. The crossing from Bosanski Samac across the River Bosna to the village of Prud, is it the village of Prud?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, the village of Prud.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we have another problem because the interpreters didn't hear you very well. What was the name of the man to whose house the command of the 4th Detachment moved?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: His name was Jovo Dusanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is Jovo Dusanovic's house in a neighbourhood called in the Bosnian language sljivak?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. This house is in the neighbourhood called sljivak which means plum orchard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you arrived in the 4th Detachment command, what time was it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: We arrived there at about 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Commander Antic tell you on that occasion and what orders did he give?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Commander Antic ordered us to go and collect weapons in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many groups were there ordered by Commander Antic to go and collect weapons in the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: There were two groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many men were in each group?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: In my group, there were about ten of us, and probably in the other group too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did each group have a person who was designated as the leader or the commander?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After all these years, can you remember who was designated the commander of your group or the leader of your group, which went to collect weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Our leader was Ljubo Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Ljubomir Simic a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the other members of your group, were they also members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everyone in the group was a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember some persons who were together with you in this group, collecting those weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Ljubo Simic. Then there was Goran Buzakovic. There was Nenad Tomasevic. Then myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If you can't remember any more, that's enough. What did Mr. Antic order you to do then? Did he explain to you the procedure you were supposed to follow when collecting weapons? What orders did he give?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Commander Antic ordered us to act in a proper manner, to treat everyone politely, to avoid conflicts, quarrels, and anything that would not be decent or proper. He said we should go to each house, ring the door bell or knock on the door, and if people had weapons and if they wanted to hand them over voluntarily, they should hand them over. We were strictly prohibited from searching houses or yards or anything in the yards. And we abided by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he prohibit you from using force or threats toward the citizens from whom you were collecting weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: There was no mention of violence at all. In fact, we were told we would be personally held responsible to him if a single incident of that kind occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that he then introduced you to persons who would monitor the performance of this order? Did he tell you who they were?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He said we would be monitored by Mr. Simo Zaric, and Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, did he designate the area or the part of town in which you were to collect weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: It was the 4th quarter of Samac or the 4th district. This is the area from the brick works along the dikes by the River Sava, Edvard Kardelja Street, in the direction of Djure Djakovica Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your knowledge, is this the largest quarter or district of the town of Samac and does it run from the dike along the bank of the River Bosna on the right hand side?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's the largest area in the town of Samac and it runs parallel to the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the river. What river?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Djure Djakovica Street is opposite the River Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were given these orders, you went into action. While conducting this action, and collecting weapons, were you escorted by an armoured combat vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were escorted by a combat vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please describe this vehicle. What kind of vehicle was it? What did it look like? How did it behave while providing security for you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: This vehicle had rubber tires. It did not have caterpillar tracks. It had three barrels and these were pointed upwards, toward the sky. And it followed some 10 or 15 metres behind us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this vehicle halt from time to time while it followed you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Of course it did, because while we were collecting weapons, the vehicle would have to halt behind us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe at any moment that the barrels of this vehicle were pointed at apartments, people's houses, or other buildings?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Not for a single moment were the barrels pointed either at houses or homes. They were simply pointed upwards, toward the sky, at an angle of perhaps some 50 degrees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Carrying out this order, did you, at a certain point in time, find yourself in Pero Bosic Street?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember whether Pero Bosic Street crosses the street that was then called Edvard Kardelja Street and is now called Czar Dusan Street?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, from Edvard Kardelja Street, you enter Pero Bosic Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you enter that street in that way?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember when you were in Pero Bosic Street, that you entered a yard belonging to Sabrija Dagovic and his brother Sulejman Dagovic? Please recount this event slowly. What did you do then, who went to the yard, what you did.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: When we turned off into Pero Bosic Street, on the right-hand side there was a house belonging to some elderly people, and there, some of the men collecting weapons wanted to enter the yard. I said that these were elderly people and that they shouldn't go there. Across the road from that house was a house belonging to Sulejman Dagovic. We knocked on the door of that house and there was no one inside. The first person to enter the yard was Goran Buzakovic, and he was followed at a distance of several metres by me and Nenad Tomasevic. Goran approached the door, the door of Esad Dagovic, also known as Ekac and he knocked on the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, stop there for a moment so we can clarify some points and then we'll continue. The house where the members of the 4th Detachment went wanting to enter the yard, did it belong to Jusuf Arnautovic and his wife Jara?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know Jusuf Arnautovic [Realtime transcript read in error "and autovic"]?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that he has no children, that he and Madam Jara live on their own?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, they live on their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned the house of Sulejman Dagovic, can you tell us whether Sulejman Dagovic's house and Sabrija Dagovic's house are in the same yard?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. They are in the same yard but Esad Dagovic's house is behind Sulejman's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, Sulejman Dagovic's house is right next to the street?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And behind Sulejman Dagovic's house, in the back of the yard, is Sabrija Dagovic's house?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, Sabrija Dagovic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does Sabrija Dagovic's house have a veranda?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So Goran Buzakovic knocked on the door of Sabrija Dagovic's house. Tell us what you saw after that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Esad Dagovic exchanged some words with him but I didn't hear exactly what they said. He took Goran Buzakovic into the basement of that house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me, looking at the transcript, page 59, line 8, reads "You know Jusuf and autovic," it should be corrected the name of the person in question according to my recollection, and the list of witnesses here should be Arnautovic, Jusuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we will clarify this right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this person called Jusuf Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are saying this simply for the sake of the transcript, to correct it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away were you when Goran Buzakovic was at the door of Sabrija Dagovic's house, when Esad Dagovic came out?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Seven or eight metres approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hear what they were saying?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't hear what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw Esad Dagovic and Goran Buzakovic going toward the basement. Did they enter the basement?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: The first to enter was Esad, followed by Goran Buzakovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did they stay there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: A very brief time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see when they came back, when they left the basement?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Goran Buzakovic was carrying a Kalashnikov with -- and two hand grenades, and with a frame, two hand grenades and a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anything shown on this occasion? Did they inspect the weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: The rifle was opened. I came a little bit nearer then, and Esad Dagovic, known as Ekac said, "Look, Goran, I didn't fire any shots from this rifle."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the barrel was inspected? Something did not enter the transcript. You said that Esad Dagovic said, "Goran, I swear by my mother no shots were fired." When we say, "By my mother," is that some sort of oath?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he took an oath on his mother that he did not fire shots. Was the pistol inspected?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, the pistol was inspected as well, the barrel. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the witness a few questions ago described Goran Buzakovic coming out of the house with some items including hand grenades, a Kalashnikov, and in the transcript, it says with a frame. That's line 7. Now, I know what a frame is but in the context of this evidence, it's meaningless so some sort of explanation of what a frame is, it might -- I assume it's some sort of weaponry and you should know precisely what sort of weaponry it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain what military weapon was brought out of the basement?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: An automatic rifle, 762, produced in Russia, with a frame or rather a frame containing a round of 35 bullets, a clip, with a clip. We don't know how many bullets were inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A frame or clip is?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: It's part of the equipment with a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Containing?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you got out of the basement, set out across the yard, and did Goran Buzakovic say anything to you after this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Goran said, "See here, he really didn't fire any shots either from the pistol or from the rifle."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you issue any sort of receipt to Esad Dagovic saying that he had handed over these weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: We didn't, because those were not our orders and we had not been given any receipt forms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. What did Goran Buzakovic do with these weapons when you got out into the street?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He put them in the military vehicle, the combat vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the place where in other instances, when you found weapons that had been left around, was that a place where you stored the weapons, where you put them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, but -- yes, because the amount of weapons were so large, we were unable to carry them all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find weapons in the yards by the road side, left at entrances to buildings, on staircases, did such things happen?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: There were weapons everywhere, all over the place, thrown into the gutters, thrown from somebody's yard into somebody else's yard, left in corridors, in apartment houses, left next to garbage cans, by yard fences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you found those weapons, I assume you collected them and put them in that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We put that in the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't conduct any investigation to discover who had left or thrown away those weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, and we didn't even write down the names of the people who did hand over weapons to us. We didn't write down who we had taken weapons from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were conducting this operation, did this military vehicle fire any shots at any moment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, no. The vehicle never fired any shots, not for a single moment, nor could it have done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. During this operation, did anybody fire shots at you, as members of the 4th Detachment, going down the street?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Nobody fired at us while we were collecting the weapons, nor were there any conflicts or even quarrels or any kind of fight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said nor could it have done, what did you mean by that? That it had no reason to fire or that it was not in good working order?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in good working order or not but it had no reason to fire and it couldn't have fired in such a small area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you, as members of the 4th Detachment, use any kind of threat or force against anyone?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Not for a single moment. There was nothing remotely like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were walking down these streets and entering other people's yards, did you and the members of the detachment feel any kind of fear?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Well, of course we did. We were out in the open. Anyone could have fired shots at us, either from the top of a building or behind a fence or from a window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think this is a good moment now for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will take our break and continue at 12.50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall, Mr. Topcagic, until when did the action of weapons collection last?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: It lasted until afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And now let's talk a little about Mr. Simo Zaric and Miroslav Tadic and about the assignment they received from the commander to control the collection of those weapons. Can you remember whether Mr. Tadic and Mr. Zaric, as this operation went on, that is seven or eight hours, came to see it and communicated with Mr. Simic as the leader of the group to see if there were any problems or whatever?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. They did come.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's clear but just in addition to clarification of which Simic we are speaking here. Just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means. We shall clear it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic whom we mention, what was his first name?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Ljubo Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ah, I see, thank you. But that is not Blagoje Simic definitely?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in Pero Bosic Street next to Sabrija Dagovic's house or rather at his son's, were Mr. Tadic and Mr. Zaric present there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Neither Mr. Tadic nor Mr. Zaric were present at the time when we were at Dagovic's house. I have no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And one other element to clear up, this armoured combat vehicle that is mentioned and which escorted you, it wasn't a tank, was it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't a tank. It was a vehicle with rubber wheels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sufficiently knowledgeable to tell a tank apart from that armoured combat vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Sure I do. A tank is a caterpillar, that is it has caterpillars and it has a barrel which is about three times as long as the other one has and it has a dome, a cupola over it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Can you only tell us approximately do you know how many weapons -- pieces of weapons were collected during that operation led and conducted by the 4th Detachment? Altogether how many pieces, roughly?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that these two groups roughly collected as many as 300 barrels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would that include, in addition to those barrels, that is military automatic weapons, other weapons such as hand grenades, bombs, ammunition, frames, clips and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: There was a lot of ammunition, about 50 or so hand grenades because they were easier to hide so they discarded them, throwing them into septic pits or sewers or whatever. Zoljas, I think we found about 20 of those. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, could it be clarified if the witness is talking about 50 or so hand grenades found in septic pits or sewers or whether they are 50 or so hand grenades found elsewhere? Because the way it reads, it may be that the witness is saying they were found in septic pits and sewers and it would be interesting to know if the 4th Detachment was looking in such places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll try to clear this up. I don't know what the interpretation is, but the answers in B/C/S are quite clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topcagic, you heard what the Prosecutor wants us to clarify. Tell us: How many hand grenades did you collect in that operation? How many hand grenades were handed over to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: About 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you search the gutters, the sewers, septic pits and other places where they could be concealed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, we did not search those but they were found later on, because the sewers would get clogged and when people came to unclog them, to clear them, that is when they found those zoljas and the clips and grenades and what not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was much later, it was much later, when clogging would occur, the people who were there, the men who came to repair, they would find hand grenades, zoljas, ammunition discarded there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, and you can still find them there, just recently in a septic pit a zolja was found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you used a term which we use, that is zolja, what actual is a zolja, what kind of weapon is it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: It is a hand held launch used to destroy armoured vehicles, buildings and bunkers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We've heard this explanation before with another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours, I just thought that it wouldn't be bad if Mr. Topcagic explained it too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, after the 18th, are you aware whether the 4th Detachment engaged in any other operation concerning the seizure of weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you finished this operation on the 18th, did the 4th Detachment again engage in the collection of weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: They did it on the 19th, too, they went out to collect weapons, but in a smaller number of places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. Now we shall close this subject. Did you have an opportunity to meet Mr. Zaric towards the end of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you met, what did Mr. Zaric tell you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He told me that with the assistance of Momcilo Petrovic, a captain, a Lieutenant Colonel Stevan Nikolic, and Makso Simeunovic, he managed to transfer imprisoned Muslims who were kept in SUP, TO in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To transfer them where?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: To Brcko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: The barracks in Brcko, the army barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the barracks, do you mean the garrison of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you what was the reason for the transfer of the detainees held in the TO and the police station?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: The reason was the ill treatment of people, people were beaten every night, forced to fornicate, teeth were pulled out, they lived in very poor -- poorly equipped rooms, with very little room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And did he also tell you on that occasion that killings had also started at the TO headquarters?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He did. He told me that he eyewitnessed, and that Sulejman Tihic was also an eyewitness when Lugar killed a man in the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this -- these things that Mr. Zaric told you, did you also have an opportunity to see for yourself the conditions under which people in the TO were detained?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I had no access to the TO building, to those rooms in the TO building, except on one occasion when Grga Zubak was in the yard. He was sitting on a chair in the sun, and a curb of the pavement had been put on his foot, and a bottle of water in front of him but so that it was without -- it would be beyond his reach. And when I saw that, I entered and it was on my own, the yard, and he addressed me by my name and said, "Fadil, please give me some water" and I tried to give him water and at that moment, a maniacal special jumped on me, his name is Laki, and he stopped me, he wouldn't allow me to give water to Grga Zubak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the conditions under which those people were there? Did anyone talk about that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Well, many talked. There was hardly any food. They were sitting on the concrete there. There was very little room and they were very numerous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever try to send them something?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I tried it often and I succeeded in doing that through some officials whom I knew personally, to send them some food, some cigarettes, and medicines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After that meeting with Mr. Zaric, where did Mr. Zaric go, if that is you know that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric went to Brcko with Toso Tutnjevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Toso Tutnjevic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Toso Tutnjevic was his driver, also a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Brcko that day?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That day with Lazar Stanisic, called Ziga, went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you go?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: We went in a private car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you and Mr. Stanisic go to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: We got some cigarettes, some food, got some undershirts, and slips, and pants, a man in Brcko called Mirkic gave it all to us, and we handed it over to the military policemen on duty who then distributed it among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you and Mr. Stanisic ever meet Mr. Zaric in the garrison in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom did you see? Just take it easy, please. Take it easy.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Of all those prisoners, I saw Osman Jasarevic, who is a distant relative of mine, and a friend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Osman Jasarevic, who is your relative, does he have a nickname, Roma?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He does, Roma yes, his nickname is Roma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see him and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He was with a military policeman outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you talk with Mr. Jasarevic, Osman Jasarevic, called Roma?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: We did but very little, he said, "Fadil, get me out of here." And I said, "Osman, all I can do is help you, to help you is to -- if you join the 4th Detachment. And then we'll see what else we can do. But the most important thing for you is to get out of detention."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And after you expounded it all to him and made these proposals to him, just take it easy, what did Mr. Jasarevic, Osman Jasarevic tell you then?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He did not accept my proposal. Or perhaps he was afraid of going back to Samac again. I don't know the reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know anything about exchanges in the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell us what it is you know.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: The first exchange took place sometime in May. The detained Serb population in Odzak was exchanged for prisoners in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where did this exchange take place?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That exchange took place with the mediation of the Red Cross in Zasavica at the Bosna River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zasavica is a village in the Bosanski Samac municipality isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at the exchange?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever present at any exchange in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was present at one exchange. It was either late June or early July near Sid in the village of Lipovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did you happen to be present at that exchange?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Everybody had friends in those exchanges -- groups that were exchanged so I had some friends. Namko [phoen] -- starting with Namko Suljic, my best friend before the war, who had already fled to Orasje and who was already commanding a company or something in the HVO, well, his wife had stayed behind, his wife Zlata had stayed behind and his two children who were under age, and I felt it was my duty to help his wife and his children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how -- how did you think you could help them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Well, to begin with, that nothing happens to them on the way to see that they do not run into any trouble, to see them off with dignity, humanely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. And your friend's name is?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Namik Suljic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Namik Suljic, thank you. And did you -- were you there in some official capacity during that exchange or was it only on your own privately that you went there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No. I had no official capacity there, but nevertheless, I was there just in case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know or -- whether Simo Zaric was also present at that exchange?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Simo Zaric was also present at that exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why Simo Zaric was present at that exchange?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He was seeing off his -- the father-in-law of his daughter, his daughter and his son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just clear this up. You are saying that Simo Zaric was seeing off the father of his son-in-law, his wife?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the mother of his son-in-law and the sister of his son-in-law, so Djuro Prgomet's -- so this is the family of Djuro Prgomet, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Djuro Prgomet's family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Simo Zaric go to that exchange? I mean what means of transport did he use?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He used his own private car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see whether there was anyone else in the car with Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did this exchange proceed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: The exchange was not carried out on that day. We stayed there the whole night and the exchange was carried out only on the following morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Zaric ask you also to stay in the vicinity of his friend with his family, Djuro Prgomet to protect them from any possible mistreatment or insults?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did, and I did this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Zaric have any official duty during this exchange?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see of official representatives at this exchange?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: There was Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anybody else? Were there any other people taking part in the exchange?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they went with us but Velimir Maslic was there when we set out, and so was Svetozar Maslic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this exchange completed successfully?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. I can mention also that there was a woman there with a disabled child and Miroslav Tadic managed to get from her the number of her sister and he even paid for a taxi and this woman with a disabled child was taken by taxi to her sister's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after this exchange, you returned to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I have completed my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution cross-examination? MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Topcagic, my name is Di Fazio, I'll ask you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution. You were in charge, I think of reconnaissance duties in the 4th Detachment, weren't you? MR. DI FAZIO: Are Your Honours getting...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we can hear. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness I just asked you, you were in charge of reconnaissance duties in the 4th Detachment, weren't you? Could you tell us if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the usher help with the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the sound be turned up a little, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Your Honours, please, if I may be of assistance -- Mr. Topcagic, please put your head set on properly. Put it on top of your head like this so they don't slip off. Can you hear better now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear my -- let me withdraw that. I'll start again. Mr. Topcagic, my name is Di Fazio, I'll ask you some questions now on behalf of the Prosecution, okay? My first question is this: I believe that you were in charge of reconnaissance duties in the 4th Detachment. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is Denis Topcagic related to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What relationship does he hold to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He is my sister's son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your nephew. And he was also in the 4th Detachment, I believe?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us whether you were officially titled commander of reconnaissance duties or whether you held some other position or whether it was called some other position?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Only the leader of the reconnaissance squad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How many --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Platoon, the interpreter corrects herself. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many members of this squad, please?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the duties of this reconnaissance platoon or squad?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Until the war broke out, we had no duties at all, until the fateful 6th [as interpreted] of April. After that, our tasks were to reconnoitre enemy positions, to reconnoitre artillery and where it was firing from, as well as enemy movements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the answer was misrecorded. He said the 16th of April, not the 6th of April. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that's an obvious. MR. DI FAZIO: I just assumed that was a typo, I didn't even bother with that. If Your Honours please I think we can assume that the witness meant the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the 4th Detachment conduct patrols in and around the town of Bosanski Samac in the period of time leading up to the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were placed in charge of reconnaissance. You were given a platoon. Members of the platoon were nominated but no reconnaissance duties were ever carried out until the 16th?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No, no reconnaissance activities or duties were carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions as to what your duties were to be, how they would be carried out and in what circumstances they would be carried out with the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Of course. In any war, reconnaissance is the same sort of duty. So they didn't need to explain to me at great length what I was to do. It was my duty to observe the enemy, enemy positions, enemy movements, and firing from enemy artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the League of Communists in 1990, did you join any other political party?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I joined the SDP party of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the party of democratic changes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to turn to the events of the night of the 16th and 17th of April, please. You say in your statement that at about midnight, the telephone rang and Savo Savic said he was on the other end. Savo Savic was a man who was well known to you, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was at that time an active-duty policeman?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I think he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That I don't know. But he was a leftist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you known him?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: For some 15 years, maybe even 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was a man who you trusted and considered to be reliable?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He was a very decent, honest man, a family man, and he was well-liked in the town. He didn't behave like a nationalist. He did his job well, and he was well-liked as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that as far as you were aware, he held no ultra nationalist or extreme nationalist views?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That's my opinion, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When he rang you at midnight and said that he wanted to come and visit you, he initially did not tell you the purpose of the visit?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And therefore, you were extremely keen to know exactly what the purpose of the visit was going to do, because it was unusual, late at night, he was a policeman. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As it was an unusual situation, it being close to midnight, and as he had not told you over the telephone the purpose of the visit, as you waited for him to arrive, you were extremely keen, extremely curious, to know precisely what the reason was for his visit. You were anxious to find out, correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: No. That's not correct. Nobody likes having a policeman arriving at midnight and neither did I, but I assumed it was something important. The fact that he was coming made me feel afraid, although we were good friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And when he arrived, he was in the presence of the man you later found out was Lugar?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any weapons. Maybe they had something in the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did they remain in the house before you left in the car to head towards Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: They didn't stay long. I can't recall exactly but the conversation was brief. When they entered the house, he introduced Lugar as a member of some sort of special unit of the MUP of Serbia, I think, I'm not sure, but some sort of special purpose policeman, and he was wearing a multi-coloured uniform. Savo was in the standard police uniform. They said to me that I was to go to Crkvina, that I was to report to some sort of Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will get to that in just a minute. Most of the talking was -- you say in your statement that most of the talking was done by Savo, Savo Savic. That is so, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Savic. It was Savo Savic who did most of the talking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Savo Savic told me -- well, first I asked him why they were coming to my house at that time of night. I asked if I had done something wrong, whether they were going to arrest me, and he just laughed and then introduced Lugar to me, saying he was from the special purpose forces of the MUP of Serbia, and that I was to go with them to some kind of Crisis Staff in Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall anything else that he said while you were still in the house? Or is that it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I asked if I could make a phone call to Simo so that I could find out where I was going and why. And then Lugar said, there is no time for that. He almost pushed me away from the telephone. He said, "Everything will become clear to you when you arrive in Crkvina."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What made you think that Simo would be able to tell you where you were going and why you were going there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: There was pressure on my house from all sides, neighbours, children in school, me at my work, in the street, in cafes, and I was fed up. I couldn't trust everyone. I even was a bit suspicious because I didn't know who this Lugar was. I suspected that perhaps their intentions were not good, and that's why I wanted to call Simo, to see if he knew anything about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for all of that but my question was this: What made you think that Simo would be able to tell you where you were going and why you were going there? What did you know or think or believe that Simo Zaric would be able to enlighten you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I was at home alone. I had to tell someone that an unknown man had come to collect me and take me somewhere. And who would I call if not him? Because he was my -- he was related to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The answer that was translated to me, Mr. Topcagic, is this: I asked if I could make a phone call to Simo so that I could find out where I was going and why. That's your answer. My question is: Why did you want to contact Simo Zaric in order to find out where you were going and why? Why Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: If I could have called anyone else at that moment, a neighbour or someone, just to let them know that I was going off somewhere in an unknown direction, because they didn't tell me -- well, they did say we were going to Crkvina but whether they were going to take me to Crkvina or somewhere else, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try again, if I can, Mr. Topcagic. You've told us that you made -- you wanted to make the phone calls to Zaric so that you could find out where you were going and why. What did you think Mr. Zaric would be able to tell you about where you were going and why?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe just to assist my learned colleague, this part of the statement is already in his statement, as paragraph 32. Perhaps this could be shown to the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: That's a completely different matter in paragraph 32 in the statement, it's a different explanation. Perhaps I'll -- I'm grateful to Mr. Lazarevic, I'll put that portion of the statement to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 32 of your statement, Mr. Topcagic, you say, "I wanted to call Simo Zaric who is my brother-in-law and tell him, tell him, that I was going to Crkvina." Can you just tell the Trial Chamber what the reasons were for ringing Simo Zaric? Firstly, was it that you wanted to tell him where you were going or is it, as you have told us today, that you wanted to find out where you were going and why?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I wanted to tell him where I was going, because how could I know whether he knew why I was going there and where I was going?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told the Chamber that this fellow Savo Savic was a policeman, he was a straightforward, honest man, he'd been your friend for some 15 years. Why not turn to the very man who had brought this person to your house and seek an explanation instead of going to Simo Zaric? Can you tell the Chamber that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: First I should say we were not friends. We were just acquaintances. I had known him for 15 or 20 years but we weren't friends. And for me to go with an unknown man off somewhere, without being sure that's where they were taking me, I had to tell someone and let them know where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told the Chamber that you trusted this fellow Savic.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: I did trust Savo Savic but I didn't know this other man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, wasn't it a golden opportunity for you to seek information from the very man who had brought this other man to your house? It was a golden opportunity for you to ask Savo Savic, who is this fellow? Why is he here? Why have you come to my house? That's -- that would have been the logical place to start, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: Do you think that a man who has killed 20 people allowed me to say what I want and do what I want, even in my own house?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't know Lugar, you'd never met him in your life. You didn't know that at the time, did you? You claim that he's a complete stranger. You had no idea as to his character.

utterances.speaker: FADIL TOPCAGIC
utterances.text: He often used the word "bre." And whenever I tried to put a question to Savo, he would interrupt me and say, bre or brother, that's none of your business. You have to go with us and even had Savo wanted to say something to me, and I think Savo himself was not sure what was going to happen in the night. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you, Mr. Topcagic, perhaps we can pick up on this topic tomorrow, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but before we rise, the Trial Chamber has been informed by the victims and witnesses unit that only particulars of two witnesses for Blagoje Simic were given to them, and late yesterday, so that they are unable to make sure that the witnesses travel and are able to be here by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Shall I give you information now, Your Honour, or to your legal officer after the -- today's hearing? What would you like?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What the Trial Chamber has observed is that there is some delay in processing these witnesses for them to be able to come because their particulars are already on the statements which have been admitted, and there appears to be no reason whatsoever why there is this delay in getting these witnesses here. As concerns their travel documents, each time counsel puts up witnesses, obviously he knows that they may come to give evidence to the Tribunal. Therefore travel documents ought to be processed long before even the orders are made. So Mr. Pantelic, make sure that your witnesses are here. We will rise now and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 1.48 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of April, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
